chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, provided he was not prevented from doing so by a need that overwhelms him, or an illness that makes him unable to perform Hajj, or a ruler who prevents him, then let him die as a Jew or a Christian.

key_terms.مَرَضٌ لَا يُطِيقُ فِيهِ الْحَجَّ: An illness that prevents enduring Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who dies without performing Hajj if they had the ability?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the gravity of neglecting the first obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam) when one possesses the requisite means (istita'ah). The metaphor of dying as a Jew or Christian serves to highlight the specific omission of this pillar rather than a total apostasy, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Kulayni to distinguish between missing a duty and rejecting faith entirely. This ruling reinforces the concept that Hajj is a fundamental condition of faith, and its unjustified delay carries severe spiritual consequences.
